name: Clonidine
summary: A blood-pressure and ADHD prescription drug that surfaces in forum stress stacks; nothing tests it for looks.
lead: Clonidine is a centrally acting alpha-2 adrenergic agonist. The US label for the tablets lists hypertension as the indication . Extended-release forms are approved for ADHD in children and adolescents .
claims: Pregnenolone plus clonidine plus cyproheptadine lowers stress and treats attention problems.

name: Zuranolone
summary: Prescription oral neurosteroid approved for postpartum depression; not an appearance compound, and carries a driving-impairment boxed warning.
lead: Zuranolone (brand name Zurzuvae) is an oral neuroactive steroid that acts as a positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors. It is a synthetic analog of the body's own neurosteroid allopregnanolone and was developed by Sage Therapeutics with Biogen. The US FDA approved it in August 2023 for postpartum depression in adults, a 14-day oral course positioned as an alternative to intravenous brexanolone.

name: Allopregnanolone
summary: Natural progesterone-derived neurosteroid behind the postpartum-depression drug brexanolone; no studied appearance use.
lead: Allopregnanolone (3alpha-hydroxy-5alpha-pregnan-20-one) is a neurosteroid the body makes from progesterone. It is a potent positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A receptors, the main inhibitory receptors in the brain. Its levels rise in stress, the luteal phase and pregnancy, and fall after delivery.

name: Kava (kavalactones)
summary: Pacific root drink and supplement for relaxation; small anxiety signal in trials, with a history of liver-safety bans.
lead: Kava is a drink and extract made from the roots of Piper methysticum, a plant domesticated in the Pacific Islands, where it is used socially and ceremonially. Its main active constituents are kavalactones, of which six account for most of its pharmacological activity. In supplement form, it is used for anxiety, stress and sleep.

name: Lavender oil capsules (Silexan)
summary: Standardized oral lavender oil sold for anxiety; some placebo-controlled data, no appearance use.
lead: Silexan is a standardized oral lavender oil preparation sold as capsules for anxiety and restlessness. It is made from Lavandula angustifolia flowers and marketed in Germany as a medicine and in the US as a supplement (CalmAid), according to a reference page.

name: Hops extract
summary: Beer-flavoring flower sold in sleep supplements; human sedative evidence is limited and appearance use is unstudied.
lead: Hops are the cone-shaped flowers of the female Humulus lupulus plant, best known for flavoring beer. Extracts are also sold in sleep and relaxation supplements, often alongside valerian or chamomile.

name: Propranolol
summary: Prescription beta blocker used off-label for performance anxiety; the forum bone-growth theory is untested in humans.
lead: Propranolol is a non-selective beta-adrenergic blocker developed by Scottish pharmacologist James Black in the 1960s, patented in 1962 and first marketed as Inderal in 1965. It is prescribed for hypertension, angina, arrhythmias, migraine prevention, essential tremor and infantile hemangioma.
claims: Propranolol calms the physical symptoms of social anxiety.
Propranolol stimulates bone growth via IGF-1 and BMP-2.

name: Tianeptine
summary: A French antidepressant with opioid-receptor activity that shows up in gray-market supplements; nothing ties it to looks.
lead: Tianeptine is an antidepressant sold under brand names such as Stablon and Coaxil in France and several other countries, where it is approved for major depressive disorder. It is not approved in the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia or by the US FDA. It was developed in the 1960s and introduced in France in 1983.

name: Tiratricol (Triac)
summary: A thyroid-hormone analogue now approved for a rare genetic disorder, once sold as a fat-burner with case reports of thyroid dysfunction.
lead: Tiratricol, also called Triac or triiodothyroacetic acid, is a synthetic thyroid hormone analogue that binds thyroid hormone receptors. It is approved in the EU and, according to a US prescribing label, in the United States as Emcitate for peripheral thyrotoxicosis in people with MCT8 deficiency (Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome).

name: Levothyroxine (T4)
summary: The standard hypothyroidism drug, which carries a boxed warning against use for weight loss.
lead: Levothyroxine is a synthetic form of thyroxine (T4), the main hormone made by the thyroid gland. It is the standard replacement therapy for hypothyroidism and is also used to suppress TSH in some thyroid cancers.
claims: Low-normal thyroid levels can be corrected with levothyroxine to improve how people look and feel.

name: Desiccated thyroid (Armour)
summary: Dried porcine thyroid containing T4 and T3, an older hypothyroidism treatment with no evidence base as a slimming aid.
lead: Desiccated thyroid extract (DTE) is dried, powdered thyroid gland, usually from pigs, taken orally for hypothyroidism. Armour Thyroid is the best-known brand. It contains both T4 and T3, in a ratio of roughly 4:1 compared with about 11:1 in humans.

name: Medroxyprogesterone acetate
summary: A prescription progestin (Depo-Provera) with only peripheral appearance uses, such as feminizing therapy and hirsutism.
lead: Medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) is a synthetic progestin sold as Depo-Provera (injectable contraceptive, DMPA) and Provera (oral). It was discovered in 1956 and introduced for medical use in the US in 1959.

name: Megestrol acetate
summary: A progestin appetite stimulant approved for cancer and AIDS wasting; nothing tested for cosmetic weight gain.
lead: Megestrol acetate is a synthetic progestin, a laboratory-made relative of the hormone progesterone, sold mainly under the brand name Megace. It is a prescription drug used to treat advanced breast and endometrial cancer and, in an oral suspension form, anorexia, cachexia or unexplained significant weight loss in people with AIDS . Its appetite-stimulating effect is the reason it appears in discussions of weight gain.

name: Cyproheptadine
summary: An allergy antihistamine prescribed off-label for appetite in children; never tested for cosmetic weight gain.
lead: Cyproheptadine is a first-generation antihistamine that also blocks serotonin 5-HT2 receptors and has anticholinergic and sedating effects. It is approved for allergic conditions such as seasonal and perennial rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis and urticaria . Increased appetite and weight gain are recognised effects of the drug, and it is prescribed off-label as an appetite stimulant, particularly in children with poor weight gain .
claims: Cyproheptadine, combined with pregnenolone and clonidine, lowers stress and addresses ADD.
Cyproheptadine is a useful appetite stimulant for gaining weight.

name: Methylphenidate
summary: An ADHD stimulant whose appetite loss is a documented side effect; never tested as a weight-loss aid.
lead: Methylphenidate, sold as Ritalin, Concerta and under many other brands, is a central nervous system stimulant prescribed mainly for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy . It is a controlled substance in most countries, including Schedule II in the US and Class B in the UK .

name: Amphetamine / Adderall
summary: A controlled stimulant that suppresses appetite as a side effect; nothing tested for weight loss or looks.
lead: Adderall is a prescription mixed-salts amphetamine product containing roughly equal parts of amphetamine aspartate, amphetamine sulfate, dextroamphetamine saccharate and dextroamphetamine sulfate, used mainly for ADHD and narcolepsy . It is a controlled substance, Schedule II in the US and Class B in the UK .
claims: Prescription ADHD stimulants can be used as an appetite suppressant to lose weight.
Adderall from an unprescribed source is often really methamphetamine.
Stimulants improve social ease and gym performance.

name: Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse)
summary: A prodrug of dextroamphetamine approved for ADHD and binge-eating disorder; its link to appearance is appetite and weight, and it is a Schedule II controlled stimulant.
lead: Lisdexamfetamine dimesylate, marketed as Vyvanse in the United States and Elvanse in Europe, is a central nervous system stimulant and a prodrug of dextroamphetamine. It is formed by attaching the amino acid lysine to dextroamphetamine, and the active drug is released after enzymatic hydrolysis in the bloodstream . It is prescribed for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children aged 6 and older and adults, and for moderate to severe binge-eating disorder (BED) in adults .

name: Quinine skin bleaching
summary: Quinine appears in reports of unregulated skin-lightening products, but no research supports it as a lightening agent and its documented effects are those of an antimalarial drug.
lead: Quinine is a cinchona alkaloid, first isolated from cinchona bark in 1820, used to treat malaria and as a bitter flavouring in tonic water . Its appearance-related interest comes from a passing mention in descriptions of unregulated skin-lightening products: Wikipedia reports that in a 1997 trafficking case in Paris, users of lightening products used preparations containing corticosteroids or quinine, as well as mercury- or bleach-based ones .

name: Ascorbyl glucoside
summary: A stabilised vitamin C derivative used in brightening and anti-ageing skincare, with a small evidence base specific to the ingredient itself.
lead: Ascorbyl glucoside (also written AA-2G; chemical name L-ascorbic acid 2-O-alpha-glucoside) is a derivative of ascorbic acid in which a glucose unit is attached to the vitamin C molecule. It is commonly used in cosmetic products as a way of delivering vitamin C to the skin .

name: Cetyl tranexamate mesylate
summary: A fat-soluble tranexamic acid ester put in serums for dark spots; early cosmetic-grade data, little independent testing.
lead: Cetyl tranexamate mesylate is a lipophilic derivative of tranexamic acid, formulated as a cosmetic ingredient for topical skin-lightening and hyperpigmentation products. It is the cetyl ester of tranexamic acid supplied as a mesylate salt.

name: Piroctone olamine
summary: A mild antifungal shampoo active for dandruff, tested head-to-head against zinc pyrithione; a scalp-health ingredient, not a hair-growth one.
lead: Piroctone olamine is the ethanolamine salt of piroctone, a hydroxypyridone-type antifungal used mainly in anti-dandruff shampoos and scalp-care products. It is sold by Clariant as Octopirox.

name: Zinc pyrithione
summary: The classic dandruff-shampoo antifungal; long used OTC in the US but barred from EU cosmetics since 2021.
lead: Zinc pyrithione (pyrithione zinc, ZPT) is a zinc coordination complex with antifungal and antibacterial properties. It is the active ingredient in many anti-dandruff shampoos and body washes and is used for seborrheic dermatitis; it is also used in antifouling paints and some textiles.

name: Selenium disulfide
summary: An old-school dandruff shampoo active (Selsun Blue); a scalp-condition treatment, not a hair-growth one.
lead: Selenium disulfide (selenium sulfide) is a topical antifungal and keratolytic agent used in shampoos for dandruff, scalp seborrheic dermatitis and tinea versicolor. It is better described as a mixture of selenium sulfide ring compounds than a single pure compound.

name: Erythrulose
summary: A raspberry-derived sugar used alongside DHA in self-tanners; claims rest on cosmetic-industry descriptions, with no trials found.
lead: Erythrulose is a four-carbon ketose sugar (a tetrose) found naturally in fruits such as raspberries and used in cosmetics as a sunless tanning ingredient. It is usually produced by microbial fermentation.

name: Silymarin (milk thistle)
summary: A milk thistle liver supplement with antioxidant chemistry; any skin or appearance role is theoretical.
lead: Silymarin is a standardised extract of milk thistle (Silybum marianum) containing flavonolignans, chiefly silibinin (silybin), along with silychristin and silidianin. It is used mainly as a liver-support supplement and has been studied for antioxidant activity.

name: Vilon
summary: A lab-studied Lys-Glu dipeptide from Russian gerontology research; mouse and cell data only, no human trials and no known link to appearance.
lead: Vilon is a synthetic dipeptide made of the amino acids lysine and glutamic acid (Lys-Glu). It was developed by the Russian gerontologist Vladimir Khavinson and colleagues at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology as part of a program on short peptide "bioregulators" . It is described as an immunomodulatory and geroprotective (anti-aging) candidate.

name: Pinealon
summary: A Glu-Asp-Arg tripeptide from Khavinson's lab marketed for brain and anti-aging use; cell and rat data, only small Russian-language human reports.
lead: Pinealon is a synthetic tripeptide with the sequence Glu-Asp-Arg (EDR) developed in Vladimir Khavinson's peptide bioregulator program. It is described as acting on the brain and nervous system, and it is discussed in nootropic and anti-aging circles.

name: Thymogen
summary: A Glu-Trp dipeptide immunomodulator derived from the calf-thymus extract Thymalin; Russian drug lineage, animal and cell data, thin human evidence.
lead: Thymogen is the brand name of a pharmaceutical based on the synthetic dipeptide L-Glu-L-Trp, which Khavinson's group isolated from the calf thymus extract Thymalin and then synthesised . It is characterised as an immunomodulator.

name: Bronchogen
summary: An Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu tetrapeptide from Khavinson's lab aimed at lung tissue; rat and cell studies only, no human trials, no appearance link.
lead: Bronchogen is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu, AEDL) developed within Vladimir Khavinson's program on short peptide bioregulators and described as directed at bronchial and lung tissue .

name: Cardiogen
summary: An Ala-Glu-Asp-Arg tetrapeptide from Khavinson's lab aimed at heart tissue; sparse rat and cell data, no human trials.
lead: Cardiogen is a synthetic tetrapeptide, Ala-Glu-Asp-Arg (AEDR), developed in the Khavinson research program and described as a cardiovascular-targeted bioregulator .
